emergence.summary: A single-gene FAH loss-of-function removes fumarylacetoacetate hydrolase, the LAST enzyme of tyrosine catabolism. FAH normally consumes (detoxifies) fumarylacetoacetate; without it, fumarylacetoacetate and succinylacetone ACCUMULATE and are hepato- and nephro-toxic -> the toxic-catabolite burden is driven UP. Read as a released BRAKE on toxic accumulation (FAH brakes the build-up; LOF releases it -> burden UP). The approved therapy is COUNTER-INTUITIVE and the kit re-derives it: nitisinone blocks the UPSTREAM enzyme HPD so the toxic intermediate is never formed (an upstream RESTRAINT), rather than restoring FAH. Definitive correction is restoring FAH (liver transplantation; FAH gene therapy investigational), with dietary tyrosine/phenylalanine restriction as adjunct. The gamma read is of the FAH locus switch structure; the disease lesion is coding, outside the promoter firewall. Magnitude [O].
emergence.emergent_axis: toxic upstream tyrosine-catabolite burden (fumarylacetoacetate / succinylacetone accumulation)

per_gene.note: FAH (fumarylacetoacetate hydrolase) is the terminal tyrosine-catabolism enzyme; it consumes fumarylacetoacetate. As a BRAKE on toxic-catabolite accumulation, its LOF RELEASES the brake -> fumarylacetoacetate and succinylacetone accumulate (toxic). The promoter gamma reads the locus switch STRUCTURE only; it does NOT encode the coding lesion (firewall). The pathological axis is the TOXIC BURDEN (it goes UP), so the corrective levers LOWER it.
